assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction broke the long-standing resolution limit set by spherical aberration in electron lenses, an invention that opened sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects across materials, chemistry and quantum-device research. It is a textbook case of a new tool opening a door to phenomena that could not be seen before, with lasting impact across physics and materials science.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider built and implemented it for the TEM, and Urban led the demonstration of aberration-corrected imaging in the late 1990s, so a three-person prize is natural. Other pioneers, notably the STEM-corrector work of Krivanek and colleagues, are not in the supplied credit and the priority question would need careful checking of the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed many times over by thousands of instruments worldwide and several decades of results; the technology is stable and the recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM corrector contribution (Krivanek and collaborators) must be recognized alongside the TEM corrector inventors; the supplied credited names do not include them.
I have a professional familiarity with this field and cannot independently verify priority details beyond my own recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions was the original experimental discovery that enabled read heads and non-volatile magnetic memory, with large technological and scientific impact, and it follows naturally from the spintronics line recognized by the GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995 and are the original experimenters. Parkin's contribution on optimizing and scaling MTJ and MgO-based devices is important, but is a later, more elegant stage and thus I would not include it on a strict original-experiment reading. Earlier low-temperature work by Julliere (not in the supplied credit) is a priority consideration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across many laboratories and in widespread commercial use for more than two decades; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely to late.
uncertainties: Whether Parkin or the MgO coherent-tunneling contributors (including Yuasa and others) must share the prize, and how to handle Julliere's 1975 low-temperature precedent.
The compound nature of the discovery (first observation, theoretical understanding, MgO improvement) may require judgment about which part is the prize-defining invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entirely new platform for correlated and topological physics with tunable flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, and spawned the field of twistronics. The experiments are a striking demonstration of a new controllable material system.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation predicted the flat-band magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states in 2018. The pairing of theory and original experiment is clean for three names, although other groups and earlier theorists could be argued.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated by many independent groups within a few years; the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field is still maturing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Unresolved nature of the superconducting pairing mechanism.
Possible additional claims, including other theory groups on moire flat bands and early fabrication contributions (such as Kim and collaborators), not in the supplied credit.
Whether the field is mature enough for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides in 2008 was an unexpected experimental finding that created a second family of high-Tc superconductors, with substantial importance for understanding unconventional pairing.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono published the original observation in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx, and the credited pair is a compact, clearly identifiable original-discovery configuration. Subsequent Tc increases by Chinese groups were important but are later developments, in line with the principle of rewarding the original experiment.
assessment.maturity: Quickly confirmed by multiple groups and a large literature exists, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and practical applications are limited so far.
uncertainties: Impact on humanity is currently mostly scientific rather than technological.
Priority questions around the quick follow-up discoveries of higher-Tc iron-based compounds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators established a new classification of quantum matter, with robust edge or surface states, and a lasting conceptual impact on condensed matter physics and materials design.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect, but Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (not in the credit list) made the decisive HgTe proposal, so the theory side is difficult. Molenkamp's group performed the original experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall edge channels in HgTe, and Hasan's ARPES work discovered the 3D topological insulator Bi1-xSbx and Bi2Se3. I would propose Kane for theory plus the two original experimenters, an imperfect but defensible choice.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed through decades of independent experiments, though technological applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and for Fu and Kane on 3D topological insulators, given the supplied names.
The compound discovery has 2D and 3D parts that might require different recognition and overlaps with the 2016 Nobel Prize in topological phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached unprecedented stability and accuracy, redefined precision measurement, and are candidates for a redefinition of the second, with applications to geodesy and tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations, and Ye pushed the clocks to record precision; the pairing is clear. Others who developed ion clocks and frequency combs have already been recognized separately.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several international labs and steadily improving performance; recognition seems timely, although the formal redefinition of the second has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the prior prizes for frequency combs and ion trapping; whether the committee sees this as an incremental advance.
Katori's role was conceptual as well as experimental, and the relative contribution of Ye's group to the original demonstrations may need review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013 and the 2017 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 opened neutrino astronomy at energies previously inaccessible, using the Antarctic ice itself as a detector, a major new instrumental door.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and its predecessors, and Karle was a long-standing leader of detector construction and analysis. Credit in a large collaboration is difficult, since many scientists and the earlier AMANDA and Baikal projects contributed, and the credited three-name list leaves ambiguity about Spiering's role.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by other analyses and by ANTARES-type experiments, but identification of sources is still limited, so source-level understanding is still developing.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution and the role of AMANDA, Baikal and other pioneers.
The sources of the neutrinos remain only partially identified, which may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire laser offered broadband tunable gain and made Kerr-lens mode-locked femtosecond pulses practical, becoming the workhorse of ultrafast science, spectroscopy and attosecond generation, with impressive downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented the Ti:sapphire laser at MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1982, and Sibbett's group demonstrated self-mode-locking (Kerr-lens mode-locking) in 1990-91. Keller's SESAM-based mode-locking is a related but distinct invention; whether it belongs in the same prize is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Universally adopted for more than three decades; the work is mature and any recognition would be late, with some overlap with the chirped-pulse and attosecond prizes.
uncertainties: Disputed boundaries between the invention of the gain medium, Kerr-lens mode locking and SESAMs.
Prior recognition of related ultrafast and laser techniques may make this appear less novel to some members.
